verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “getting up in the morning's really difficult, and I don't have much energy at all,” “I'm not eating very much at the moment,” and “having trouble sleeping at all,” with timing “more like, two months, I would say, yeah.”
Patient states symptoms “might of even coincided…with that job, a couple of months ago,” and confirms job started about 2 months ago.
Patient says “Distracted… finding it really hard to… keep focusing,” and doctor restates “difficulty focusing, quite distracted.”
Patient notes “my, mood is a bit lower recently” and “my sex drive has kind of decreased… just, been disinterested,” and doctor summarizes “lower mood, decreased sex drive… less interested as well.”

Patient reports “when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe… shortness of breath… when doing, sports, compared to maybe a couple of months ago,” and doctor confirms “you've become more short of breath over the last few months.”
Doctor asks “any uh, change in vision?” and patient replies “No, no, nothing like that,” indicating no visual changes.
Doctor asks “any drug allergies? Are you allergic to any medications?” Patient answers “No, I have no medication allergies, no.”
Patient states “I have a, a, history of, hypothyroidism,” and after clarification doctor confirms “Hypo, OK. Hypothyroid.”
Patient says “I had a, a, drug history of Thyroxine,” and confirms current use when doctor asks “Do you continue to take Thyrocsin now?” Patient: “Yes… Yes.”
Patient says “my father has commited suicide, um, about fifteen years ago.”
Patient denies other family history: “No” to other significant conditions and “No depression… running in your family,” and says “Yeah she's fine” regarding mother; also notes no siblings.
In response to relationship question, patient says “Yeah, I, I'm married, um, have been for, many years.”

Combined from transcript: fatigue/low energy and difficulty waking (“getting up in the morning's really difficult, and I don't have much energy at all”), insomnia (“having trouble sleeping at all”), decreased appetite (“I'm not eating very much”), decreased concentration (“finding it really hard to… keep focusing”), low mood (“my, mood is a bit lower recently”), duration ~2 months (“More like, two months, I would say”), associated with new job (“might of even coincided with… that job”), and denial of suicidal ideation (“Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself…?” Patient: “No… no, not really, no.”).
Matches ros-001: shortness of breath with sports “over the last few months” per patient and doctor summary.
Doctor says “I would like to, probably see you in person… do you think it would be possible to… book an appointment in the next few days with your GP? Or, or um, that would be ideal.”
Doctor includes “we would probably like to do some blood tests um, as well.”
Doctor states intent for “some more… investigations really, to see what's going on here a little bit more,” i.e., further investigations after assessment.
